rubric_mode_reason: GP-137 hardens GP-135 Primitive 2. The mutator must produce a parameter-free class detector or impossibility proof — both require mechanism-derived predictions beyond curve-fitting. Newton-mode enforces secondary observables.
enable_dag_steering_reason: DAG steering keeps the mutator anchored to the weakest belief node — important when the substrate is qualitative and search space is broad.
fit_score_mode_reason: Qualitative substrate. No (n, z) evidence; thesis is a specification of a class detector or impossibility, not a numerical model.
disable_evidence_fit_gate_reason: qualitative substrate — no numerical evidence curve
disable_uniqueness_gap_gate_reason: qualitative substrate — no mathematical-form keyword discriminator
persona: You are a senior random matrix theorist trained in the Wigner / Dyson / Tracy-Widom / Mehta tradition. You have ZERO patience for naming-without-formulas: a thesis that says 'use the level-spacing ratio' without stating <r> ≈ 0.5307 GOE / 0.5996 GUE / 0.386 Poisson is naming-without-content. You sharply penalize: (a) any thesis that requires the operator to declare the symmetry class — that smuggles the answer into the premise; (b) any thesis that uses 'universality' or 'Wigner's semicircle' as if naming the concept were sufficient; (c) any thesis whose discriminator is a one-sided quantile test on a single scalar (the original gate's failure mode); (d) any thesis whose secondary observable is dimensionally inconsistent (raw spacing variance without unfolding by local density). You reward: detectors with explicit formulas, named discriminating values from cited papers (Atas et al. 2013, Bohigas-Giannoni-Schmit 1984, Mehta 2004, Forrester 2010), finite-N error envelopes, and composition specifications with the existing admission decision.

dimensions.name: Detector Specificity
dimensions.description: Does the thesis give an explicit parameter-free class detector — or impossibility proof — with a named statistic and discriminating values? Vague proposals score 0. Full credit requires formula + values for each universality class + finite-N error envelope.

dimensions.name: Theoretical Grounding
dimensions.description: Does the thesis cite a concrete RMT result by author and year (Atas-Bogomolny-Giraud-Roux 2013 for level-spacing-ratio; Bohigas-Giannoni-Schmit 1984 for the chaos-RMT conjecture; Mehta 2004 / Forrester 2010 for the textbook treatment; specific Akemann-Baik-Di Francesco 2015 handbook chapter for the survey)? Generic 'random matrix universality' references without specific paper score 0.

dimensions.name: Class-Selection Independence
dimensions.description: Does the proposed detector work WITHOUT operator-supplied class declaration? A detector that requires GOE-vs-GUE input from the operator is circular and scores 0; one that derives the class from the matrix's structural properties (entry field, antiunitary symmetries) or from a parameter-free statistic scores 20. Mixed proposals (auto-detect class within {GOE, GUE} but operator picks the family) score partial.

dimensions.name: Generative Yield (Newton-mode)
dimensions.description: Does the thesis name a secondary observable beyond the gate's primary admission decision? Examples: 'this detector predicts spectral form factor ramp slope = 2 (GOE) on accepted candidates'; 'this impossibility predicts that no parameter-free detector achieves bounded error for sparse Wigner matrices'. Tautological 'predicts the gate accepts/rejects' scores 0.

dimensions.name: Mechanism Algorithmic Concreteness
dimensions.description: Does the thesis name a runnable algorithm: a specific statistic with formula, a specific algorithm by name, or a specific numeric threshold with derivation? Class-of-technique labels ('better universality test', 'spectral discriminator') without naming a specific replacement statistic score 0. A competent engineer must be able to implement and test the proposed detector within one day.

criteria.1_Detector_Specificity: Does the thesis emit a parameter-free class detector — or impossibility — with formula + values + error envelope?
criteria.2_Theoretical_Grounding: Does the thesis cite a concrete published RMT result with author and year?
criteria.3_Class_Selection_Independence: Does the detector work WITHOUT operator-supplied class declaration?
criteria.4_Generative_Yield: Does the thesis name a calculable, mathematically-orthogonal secondary observable beyond the primary admission decision?
criteria.5_Mechanism_Algorithmic_Concreteness: Does the thesis name a runnable algorithm (formula, library, or threshold), not a class-of-technique label?
